cases.obligation: Curriculum alone owns canonical AssessmentDefinition truth.
Learning alone owns learner-specific AssessmentAttempt truth.
AssessmentDefinition cannot be mutated through an AssessmentAttempt operation.
Attempt creation or submission cannot directly create mastery.
A scoring observation is not automatically a finalized score.
A finalized score remains evidence input and not mastery truth.
Shared Assurance retains generic calibration authority.
Shared Assurance retains generic fairness and drift authority.
Generic model runtime or provider transport cannot write canonical Learning score truth.
Chat or an LLM cannot become a second assessment or scoring authority.
Generic evidence storage cannot decide score meaning or mastery.
Book, Documents, Programming, and unrelated domains cannot enter canonical assessment semantics.
Attempt pins exact AssessmentDefinition version.
Attempt pins exact skill and criterion versions required by policy.
Attempt pins exact rubric and scoring-policy version.
Attempt records assessment mode and permitted assistance conditions.
Attempt records relevant accommodation conditions without treating them as automatic invalidation.
Submission identity is distinct from attempt identity and score identity.
Later Curriculum changes do not silently reinterpret historical attempts.
Later rubric changes require explicit regrade or successor handling.
Same attempt operation plus same semantic payload replays idempotently.
Same operation identity plus different payload fails deterministically.
Concurrent attempt updates cannot overwrite newer owner-valid state.
Restart reconstructs exact attempt and submission lineage from durable state.
Scorer output begins with explicit non-final standing unless policy requirements are satisfied.
Finalization binds exact attempt and submission identity.
Finalization binds exact rubric and scoring-policy versions.
Finalization records exact scorer or model identity when automation participates.
Finalization cannot proceed when required Assurance standing is unknown or stale.
Finalization cannot proceed when required human review is incomplete.
Model self-confidence alone cannot authorize consequential score finalization.
Score correction creates explicit successor lineage rather than destructive overwrite.
Regrade preserves original and successor definition/rubric/model contexts.
Learner challenge cannot directly edit a finalized historical score.
Successful challenge may authorize a new result only through governed successor handling.
Corrected score triggers downstream reprojection as a successor rather than rewriting mastery history.
AI scoring is allowed only when the exact scoring policy permits its role.
AI advisory output cannot masquerade as authoritative final score.
Exact model and configuration version are preserved when material to scoring.
Exact prompt or scoring configuration version is preserved when material.
AI score binds immutable submission identity or digest/reference.
AI output cannot become mastery directly.
AI score outside approved response type or domain fails closed or requires review.
AI score under unsupported language or population standing fails closed or requires review when policy requires.
Provider metadata cannot substitute for model-governance standing.
AI feedback generation remains separate from authoritative score finalization.
Material model or human disagreement triggers policy-defined review rather than silent averaging.
No scorer wins a disagreement merely because it reports higher confidence.
Required calibration or validation standing is scoped to intended assessment use.
Valid standing for one rubric or use does not automatically transfer to another.
Acceptable overall accuracy cannot by itself establish fairness.
Unresolved relevant subgroup disparity can block consequential model scoring according to policy.
Sensitive attributes are not copied into canonical Learning state merely to evaluate model fairness.
Material model-version change invalidates stale standing where Assurance policy requires requalification.
Material rubric or scoring-configuration change triggers required re-evaluation standing.
Detected performance or subgroup drift causes fail-closed, fallback, or review behavior per policy.
High-consequence use can require human review even when a model returns a score.
Out-of-domain or ambiguous response can require human review.
Human-review disposition preserves exact evidence, rubric/policy version, and reason codes.
Human adjudication preserves original scorer output lineage rather than deleting it.
Assessment definition or policy explicitly governs permitted tools/help/AI where relevant.
Known AI/tool assistance conditions remain attached to attempt/result interpretation.
Permitted AI use is not automatically treated as misconduct.
Prohibited assistance cannot be asserted from raw suspicion alone.
AI-detector output cannot be sole misconduct or evidence-invalidation authority.
Raw chat, device, or provider telemetry cannot silently invalidate an attempt.
Authorized accommodation is not automatically interpreted as weaker evidence.
Instructional scaffold, accommodation, ordinary tool, and prohibited assistance remain distinguishable.
Independent-performance interpretation follows the intended construct rather than a universal no-tools rule.
Integrity review preserves evidence and adjudication lineage.
No new authoritative external score callback is invented by 001I.
Raw external scorer callback or payload cannot become canonical Learning score truth.
Successful transport delivery does not imply score finalization.
Unresolved external score ingress remains pending, review-required, or blocked rather than guessed.
Duplicate provider delivery cannot create duplicate semantic score outcomes.
Provider timeout or model outage yields governed fallback, review, or pending state rather than synthetic score.
Lost response after score commit is reconciled to the existing result rather than recommitted.
Attempt/result mutation, operation receipt, and owner outbox commit atomically where the runtime contract requires them.
Mastery consumes only owner-valid finalized assessment evidence when finalization is required.
Adaptive next-action policy cannot consume raw model/provider scoring output as authoritative score.
Consequential result explanation exposes definition/rubric/scorer/model/review/assistance standing without requiring chain-of-thought.
Software qualification PASS cannot be labeled psychometric validity PASS.
Model calibration or fairness evaluation cannot be labeled educational-effectiveness PASS.
Changed assessment/scoring executable bytes require fresh exact-subject qualification; historical PASS does not transfer.
